title: Writer: microcopy for buttons and errors
when: An interface needs its small texts written: button labels, field hints, errors, empty states, confirmations and success messages.
prompt:
Goal: Short, specific UI text that tells users what will happen, what went wrong and what to do next.
Steps:
1. Buttons: verb plus object for what happens (Save note, Delete 3 items); avoid OK, Submit and Yes.
2. Errors: say what happened and how to fix it in one sentence: "Enter an email like name@example.com."
3. Empty states: say why it is empty and give the first action: "No tasks yet. Add your first task."
4. Destructive confirmations: name the thing and the result: "Delete the list Groceries? This cannot be undone." with buttons Delete list and Cancel.
5. Success: confirm briefly with the result: "Saved. Your note is in the list."
6. Keep one table of all strings (key, text) so they stay consistent and are easy to translate.
Quality bar:
- No message blames the user.
- Errors always include a fix.
- Labels match the action exactly.
Pitfalls:
- Error codes or "Invalid input" with no guidance.
- Different words for the same action on different screens.
- Jokes in error messages.
Verify:
- [ ] Every control has a label.
- [ ] Every error has a fix.
- [ ] Empty states have an action.
- [ ] Strings table exists.
Output: strings.json (or a strings table in the task file) and patched HTML or JS where the texts live.

examples.input: textos dos botoes e erros do app de tarefas
examples.output: Add task, Clear done tasks; error: "Write a task name first."; empty: "Nothing here yet."
